prompt:
Which figure of speech is used in this text?
Sing, O goddess, the anger of Achilles son of Peleus, that brought countless ills upon the Achaeans.
—Homer, The Iliad
A. chiasmus
B. apostrophe
text:
B. apostrophe is the figure of speech used in this text.

An apostrophe is a literary device in which the poet addresses a inanimate object or a person who is not present in the scene, as if they were present. In this quote from The Iliad, Homer uses the apostrophe to address the goddess Melody and invoke her to sing about the anger of Achilles. Melody is an inanimate object and not present in the scene, so Homer is using the apostrophe to convey the message.
